Payable transfer wrapper that forwards to transferFrom with msg.sender as the source.

Pure helper computing the deterministic pair address from two token addresses.

Caller supplied by the transaction; used for ownership checks, allowance spending and transfers.
Miner influenced timestamp used to build the addLiquidityETH deadline.
Transaction origin; used directly as owner and as a beneficiary of unlimited allowances during deployment.

edges.reason: Owner is assigned from tx.origin during construction, so a phishing intermediary becomes the privileged owner.
tx.origin receives an unlimited allowance on the pair, making the deployer transaction origin a trusted spender.
The constructor stores the pair address returned by pairOfTokens into uniPair.
The constructor calls pairOfTokens to derive the pair address.
transfer immediately delegates execution to transferFrom using msg.sender as source.
caller address flows from msg.sender into the transfer source.
msg.sender controls which allowance slot is read and decremented inside transferFrom.
msg.sender is used as the allowance owner in approve.
approve writes an attacker chosen spender/value into the allowance mapping.
transferFrom mutates the allowance mapping of the source account.
Allowance and balance updates in transferFrom use raw -=/+= without SafeMath.
checkBots modifier executes an external low-level call before the state mutations of transferFrom.
The modifier performs a low-level call to stopTheBots with caller supplied from/to/value arguments.
The external stopTheBots call can re-enter transferFrom before its balance/allowance updates complete.
delegate is guarded by require(msg.sender == owner).
An owner supplied address and payload are executed via delegatecall in this contract's context.
The delegatecall target executes arbitrary code that can call back into delegate or other functions.
distribute is restricted to msg.sender equal to owner.
The owner-only require gates the whole distribute routine.
distribute performs a low-level external call to stopTheBots with an attacker controlled recipient array.
The stopTheBots call can re-enter distribute and distort the airdrop balances.
distribute assigns balances directly to arbitrary addresses without any supply accounting.
Balance assignments in the distribute loop bypass SafeMath and consistency checks.
list is restricted to msg.sender equal to owner.
The owner-only require gates list, including liquidity addition and airdrop.
totalSupply is read to compute the owner's minted share in list.
list writes balances for this contract, the caller and arbitrary recipients without SafeMath.
list mutates balances directly and never reconciles against totalSupply.
pancakeRouter is used to add liquidity during listing.
list makes an external payable call to the router before performing the airdrop loop.
The liquidity deadline is block.timestamp + 600, making the call dependent on miner controlled time.
The router call can re-enter list while balances are already credited but the airdrop loop has not run.
list performs a second low-level call to stopTheBots inside the token distribution flow.
The stopTheBots call can re-enter list and re-run liquidity and airdrop logic.
pairOfTokens hashes token addresses; no balance mutation is performed here.
transferFrom relies on owner style approvals and the checkBots gate for authorisation of transfers.
distribute references state but relies on the low-level bot contract call rather than the router.

normalization_plan.reason: Constructor-only address argument used to initialise stopTheBots; has no independent semantic role.
Recipient argument only meaningful inside the transfer wrapper.
Amount argument forwarded straight into transferFrom; absorbed by the transfer function node.
Source account argument is consumed only by transferFrom balance and allowance logic.
Destination argument is consumed only by transferFrom balance logic.
Amount argument participates in the checkBots call and unchecked balance arithmetic of transferFrom.
Spender argument is written only into the allowance mapping by approve.
Allowance value argument exists only as the value written by approve.
Delegatecall target argument is used only by the delegate function.
Calldata argument is executed only by the delegate function.
Local flag is the direct result of the unsafe delegatecall operation.
Token argument is only used for the deterministic pair hash inside pairOfTokens.
Token argument is only used for the deterministic pair hash inside pairOfTokens.
Ordering temporary that exists only inside pairOfTokens.
Ordering temporary that exists only inside pairOfTokens.
Returned hash result produced exclusively by pairOfTokens.
Recipient array is used only inside distribute and its external bot call.
Amount argument is assigned to every recipient only within distribute.
Loop counter scoped entirely to the distribute function.
Liquidity token amount argument is meaningful only inside list.
Recipient array is consumed only by the list airdrop loop.
Amount array is consumed only by the list airdrop loop.
Loop counter scoped entirely to the list function.
Source argument is encoded only into the bot-protection call performed by the modifier.
Destination argument is encoded only into the bot-protection call performed by the modifier.
Amount argument is encoded only into the bot-protection call performed by the modifier.
Success flag is the direct return of the low-level stopTheBots call.
Return data of the low-level stopTheBots call is captured but never decoded.
